quote: Large language models (LLMs) have become indispensable in modern applications, powering a wide array of systems from chatbots to content generators.
outputs: generated responses to prompts involving factual knowledge editing, such as answering questions after knowledge updates

quote: Reliability assesses how accurate the edit is performed [...] Generality evaluates the model's capacity to apply the edit correctly [...] Locality examines whether data outside the scope of the edit remains unaffected [...] Portability evaluates the robustness of the generalization of the edit [...] Correct Answer Probability (CAP) measures the probability that the model generates the correct answer [...] Direct Probability (DP) assesses the model's likelihood of producing the edited knowledge [...] Editing Overfit Score (EOS) evaluates whether the model overfits [...] Answer Modify Score (AMS) measures unintended interference [...]
We evaluate using metrics such as Reliability, Generality, Locality, Portability, CAP, OAP, DP, EOS, and AMS ...
We next introduce the key probability-based metrics used to quantify overfitting.
